cells.tense: You are walking on from what you gathered, and your attention lands where it needs to be.
cells.act: sit still until the calibration settles
cells.ask: Sit down once tomorrow with nothing in your hands, ten minutes, and let what matters sort itself — no list, no decision.
cells.core:
You've come through something, and you're still walking. What gets your attention has shifted: the old anchors are behind you, and the new ones arrive obvious before anyone explains them. You don't need to argue for why a thing counts. You just see it, and it shows in how you spend your time — the people you're building the next stretch with keep getting your real attention, and the balance holds.

To keep it, spend some of that attention on rest. Once tomorrow, sit with nothing in your hands and let what matters sort itself. Not a review of the week, not a decision — ten minutes of stillness that settles the machinery. Seeing clearly got you here; this is what keeps the receiver pointed at what counts instead of at what's loud.
cells.sheetLine: You see what counts. Let it rest on purpose.

cells.tense: You are still holding up something that ended, and the next gate is coming.
cells.act: build the first new thing from what the clearing showed
cells.ask: Make one small concrete thing that isn't about the past — a page, a shelf, a first step of a walk with them — nothing more than that.
cells.core:
You're bracing at the next threshold before it arrives. Your attention keeps going back to what's ending, hunting for the smallest wrong turn. You read the situation before anyone has spoken and start rearranging it so nobody has to walk through the discomfort — and that's the exact thing slowing the walk. The connection you're trying to keep is being managed at a distance, and it can feel that.

Build something small from what the threshold cleared. One page, one shelf, the first step of some small thing with the people you're moving toward. Skilled, real, and nowhere near as big as you think. You don't need a new life. You need something real to put your hands on while the next gate opens.

cells.tense: You are still facing a door the record puts behind you, planning without moving.
cells.act: work the pattern through to its logic
cells.ask: Take something you keep trying to think clean and work it through to its actual end on paper — what follows from what, nothing skipped.
cells.core:
A way of holding people already ended, and it still gets your attention. You keep the old fit nearby — their mood, what they'd make of what you're reading — and you do it in ways that don't look like anything, as if that fit still decides how you spend your hours. The walking-on path exists in your life, shared ground with people who are already here. You talk about it as quietly managed space instead.

Take something you keep trying to think clean and work it through to its actual end on paper. What follows from what, nothing skipped. Not to reach a verdict; to see whether any of the thinking still carries weight. When it doesn't, you have a fact instead of a fog. That's a workable form of the door, and it's small enough to hold. Let what you count decide where your hands go next.

cells.tense: Your clear read is already running, and you keep crediting it to instinct.
cells.ask: The moment you're about to call your read instinct, leave it unlabeled instead — no tuning, no fixing, an hour of leaving it as is.
cells.core:
Your clearest read is right there, and you keep telling the story as though it's instinct or timing. You see what matters before anyone has explained it, and you've been doing it so long it feels like luck. That happens without you noticing you're doing it, so when something goes well you give the credit elsewhere — and what you build next comes from what you think did the steering.

For an hour, stop adjusting. The moment you're about to hand your read over to the word instinct, leave it, don't tune it, don't fix it. An hour of that is how the touch comes back to the hand that already has it. Then your account of what you're doing matches what you're actually doing, and the next step gets built on the true thing.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is the Too Little cell's 'a door that's already behind you' — the record supports a threshold of meaning the person hasn't stepped through, not an event with a date or a shape. The reader could reasonably say the going-on-toward-deeper-connection and the leaving-behind reading of this card belong to people and groups, but I've kept every ask about what this one person attends to, which stands on its own. The asks survive my read being wrong: each is one bounded move, useful whether or not the threshold is accurate, and never conditions anything on the diagnosis being right. The sentence that serves me rather than them is the exclamation-mark aphorism 'Some things get sharper by being handled less.' I've cut it and used a plain version of the idea instead.
